clues: A prominent linear bone marking on the longest bone of the body.
It serves as a major attachment site for vasti, adductors, and intermuscular septa.
It is the rough vertical ridge along the posterior shaft of the femur.
A palpable bony elevation on the anterior lower limb near the knee.
It transmits quadriceps extension force from a strong ligament.
It is the anterior proximal tibial prominence where the patellar ligament attaches.
A large tarsal bone in the hindfoot.
It supports the talus and forms the posterior pillar of the foot arch.
It is the heel bone where the calcaneal tendon inserts.
A clinical test/sign assessing hip abductor function and pelvic stability.
It appears when standing on one leg and the opposite hip drops.
It reflects gluteus medius or minimus weakness on the supporting side.
The largest nerve in the human body.
It arises from the sacral plexus and divides into tibial and common fibular parts.
It usually exits below piriformis and supplies posterior thigh, leg, and foot.
A powerful four-headed muscle group of the anterior thigh.
Its tendon incorporates the patella and continues as the patellar ligament.
It is the chief extensor of the knee joint.
A subfascial triangular space in the upper anterior thigh.
It is bounded by the inguinal ligament, sartorius, and adductor longus.
It contains the femoral nerve, femoral artery, and femoral vein.
A major nerve of the lumbar plexus (L2 to L4) entering the medial thigh.
It passes through the obturator canal to reach its target compartment.
It innervates most adductor muscles of the thigh.
A deep continuation of the main arterial trunk of the lower limb.
It lies closest to the femur and knee capsule inside a diamond-shaped fossa.
It arises at the adductor hiatus and divides into anterior and posterior tibial arteries.
A branch of the common fibular nerve entering the front of the leg.
It runs with the anterior tibial artery and continues to the first web space.
It innervates ankle dorsiflexors and toe extensors in the anterior leg.
A gait and posture finding caused by anterior leg muscle weakness.
The affected foot hangs plantarflexed and catches or drags during swing phase.
It results from inability to dorsiflex the ankle, often after fibular nerve injury.
A broad flat muscle in the superficial posterior calf.
Unlike gastrocnemius, it attaches only to leg bones rather than the femur.
It joins gastrocnemius at the calcaneal tendon and aids posture and venous return.
A strong plantar ligament in the sole of the foot.
It stretches from the calcaneus to the navicular bone.
It supports the head of the talus and helps maintain the medial longitudinal arch.
One of two terminal branches of the tibial nerve in the foot.
Its motor and sensory pattern resembles the median nerve in the hand.
It supplies medial sole skin and muscles such as abductor hallucis and FDB.
An intracapsular ligament inside the knee joint.
It runs from the anterior tibial intercondylar area toward the lateral femoral condyle.
It prevents anterior displacement of the tibia on the femur.
A short muscle forming the inferior floor of the popliteal fossa.
Its tendon passes intracapsularly relative to the lateral meniscus.
It rotates the femur or tibia to unlock the extended knee joint.
A very strong Y-shaped ligament over the front of the hip joint.
It attaches from the ilium to the intertrochanteric line of the femur.
It resists hyperextension of the hip joint during upright standing.
The longest superficial vein in the human body.
It passes anterior to the medial malleolus and ascends the medial leg and thigh.
It pierces the saphenous opening to drain into the femoral vein.
A large branch arising from the femoral artery in the femoral triangle.
It gives off circumflex and perforating branches.
It is the chief arterial supply to the thigh muscles and femur.
An opening in the distal tendinous part of a large medial thigh muscle.
It connects the adductor canal with the posterior knee region.
The femoral artery passes through it to become the popliteal artery.
